justification: Corrects served regulatory numbers in dcp_setback_controls, the product's core table: canada_bay 701 served a rear setback 4x under the actual control; ryde's and burwood's general primaries existed nowhere so no gate could examine them; fairfield served Chapter-5C narrow-lot values under secondary_dwelling. Wrong served numbers are the silent-liability class, which is the critical tier's definition. Standard would understate it; there is no higher tier.

falsifiable_check.passes_when: every stored control value is derivable from its own source_text by a named rule or sits in the shrink-only baseline; no served row carries a self-declared assumption; the SQL CHECK constraint, the Python CANONICAL_CONTROL_TYPES set and (via the database-marked test) every distinct control_type in production agree; and a quote at exactly the 400-char extractor cap is TRUNCATED_EVIDENCE regardless of its final character
falsifiable_check.fails_when: a repaired row's quote no longer supports its value (the exact camden-690 regression: value corrected, old quote kept — the gate fired on it within minutes); the baseline is grown without --allow-growth; secondary_street_setback is removed from either side of the vocabulary sync; or the punctuation exemption is reintroduced into evidence_is_truncated
falsifiable_check.demonstrated_failing: test_a_quote_at_the_limit_is_truncated_even_ending_in_punctuation asserts evidence_is_truncated('x'*399 + '.') — on the pre-change code this exact assertion fails (the old code exempted punctuation-terminated 400-char quotes), which is the escape Sol identified. Conversely test_a_short_quote_is_never_truncated fails if the fix overshoots to length-independent truncation. Live DB before/after: canada_bay 701 value_min 1.5->6.0 with the C9 quote; restoring the backup quote while keeping 6.0 makes the checker exit non-zero.
falsifiable_check.mutation_evidence: evidence_is_truncated hardcoded False -> the mid-word and punctuation tests fail; hardcoded True -> the short-quote/None/empty tests fail. Dropping secondary_street_setback from CANONICAL_CONTROL_TYPES -> test_migration_matches_python_vocabulary fails AND test_every_db_control_type_is_canonical fails against production (20 live rows). Reverting 701's value in the DB while keeping the C9 quote -> 1.5 is not derivable from the C9 quote and the row is not baselined -> checker exits non-zero.

pre_impl.existing_data: dcp_setback_controls (1,069 -> 1,071 rows): 8 rows updated by id with per-row pre-state guards, 2 inserted; backup tables dcp_setback_controls_cb701_repair_20260803 and dcp_setback_controls_missing_primary_20260803. Also the shrink-only checker baseline (41 -> 38) and the control_type CHECK constraint (migration 054, already applied 2026-08-02 — file-side sync only here).
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: If a row's live state no longer matches the recon pre-state, its guarded UPDATE matches 0 rows: the cb701 script exits 2 after printing the divergence; repair_missing_primary_controls rolls back the ENTIRE transaction on any mid-apply guard miss, so a partial adjudication cannot be committed. Dup-checked inserts skip instead of duplicating.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: Updates touch exactly the 9 named ids (701, 680, 681, 682, 691, 707, 714, 715, 716); inserts add ids 1175/1176. No blanket UPDATE exists anywhere in the diff. The vocabulary/display-map changes apply at read time but only add a mapping for a type that previously fell through to the 'Other' bucket.
pre_impl.external_source_error: No external API in the write path. The evidence source is local PDFs in data/dcps/; where a source was unavailable the ruling recorded UNVERIFIABLE and no row was written (georges_river 570 and marrickville 895 are exactly this: left open, no write).
pre_impl.frontend_type: No TS type change: StructuredControl.control_type is string. The new slug gets CONTROL_CATEGORIES/CONTROL_TYPE_LABELS entries; before this it rendered via the existing '|| Other' fallback, after it renders under Setbacks. SEE CATEGORY_MAP gains one key.
pre_impl.user_failure_mode: If a repair were wrong the user would see a wrong setback number with a quote that supports it — which is why every write carries the verbatim clause read from the PDF (rule 2b) and the checker verifies value-from-quote derivability for all rows on every push. needs_review flags (682, 716) surface as under_review, not as numbers.

functions.name: build_plan
functions.input: an open psycopg2 cursor, used to SELECT the live dcp_setback_controls row 701 with its value, currency, quote and condition at plan time
functions.output: the pre-state row tuple if it still matches the recon pre-state, else None (caller reports already-done/diverged)
functions.if_none: row absent raises SystemExit before any write; a None return prints the live row and plans zero writes

functions.name: narrowing_hits
functions.input: the row's control_type slug plus its source_text string, which may be empty or hold no narrowing terms at all
functions.output: narrowing-term matches that are NOT inherent to the control type; empty list means the row is not B-flagged
functions.if_none: empty text yields no matches — row simply not flagged; condition None is normalised at the call site

functions.name: evidence_is_truncated
functions.input: source_text (str or None) from any controls row
functions.output: bool — True when the quote sits at the 400-char extractor cap (cut, or indistinguishable from one)
functions.if_none: None coerces to '' and returns False — absence of a quote is MISSING_SOURCE_TEXT's job, not truncation's

values.nullable: no — build_plan already required a non-None quote containing the side-table marker at exactly 400 chars
values.guard_at: scripts/repair_canada_bay_rear_setback.py:184 (WHERE source_text = %s AND condition IS NULL — IS NULL, never = NULL, for the nullable column)
values.if_missing: guard matches 0 rows, script exits 2 with the rollback already printed; nothing half-written

values.nullable: yes — most rows carry NULL condition
values.if_missing: treated as unconditioned, which is exactly the defect the B-list reports

queries.purpose: guarded single-row repair of canada_bay 701 (value + quote + condition in one statement, rule 2b)
queries.where_clause: id = %s AND control_type = 'rear_setback' AND value_min = %s AND is_current = TRUE AND source_text = %s AND condition IS NULL
queries.if_zero: rowcount != 1 -> exit 2, PARTIAL APPLY printed, backup + rollback already on record
queries.if_wrong: cannot address a different row: id is the primary key and every other predicate pins the observed pre-state

queries.purpose: plan which of the 8 adjudicated updates still match their pre-state guards
queries.where_clause: id = %s AND <per-row guard: control_type + value_min + is_current/needs_review pre-state + quote shape>
queries.if_zero: row is reported as already done/diverged and excluded from the write plan — reruns are idempotent
queries.if_wrong: a guard matching a mutated row is prevented by pinning value, type, currency and quote prefix together; any mid-apply miss rolls back the whole transaction

queries.purpose: dup-check before each INSERT of a missing primary
queries.where_clause: lga = %s AND dev_type = %s AND control_type = %s AND COALESCE(condition,'') = COALESCE(%s,'')
queries.if_zero: insert proceeds (the control is genuinely absent — the MISSING_PRIMARY finding)
queries.if_wrong: worst case a duplicate is skipped, never double-inserted; deliberately currency-blind so a retired twin still blocks a blind re-add and forces a human look

break_it.scenario: Concurrent edit changes 701 between plan and apply (another session repairs or retires it first)
break_it.what_happens: unguarded, the write would clobber the other session's repair with stale values
break_it.how: repair_canada_bay_rear_setback.py:176 — UPDATE pinned to the exact planned pre-state incl. the full old source_text; rowcount != 1 exits 2
break_it.repro: UPDATE dcp_setback_controls SET value_min = 9.9 WHERE id = 701; then python scripts/repair_canada_bay_rear_setback.py --apply -> 'pre-state no longer matches', nothing written

break_it.scenario: Value corrected but the quote still supports the OLD value (the camden-690 failure, rule 2b)
break_it.what_happens: the row looks verified while its evidence contradicts it — worse than the original defect
break_it.how: the same UPDATE statement writes value_min AND source_text AND condition together; the push-time checker then requires 6.0 derivable from the stored quote
break_it.repro: UPDATE dcp_setback_controls SET source_text = (SELECT source_text FROM dcp_setback_controls_cb701_repair_20260803 WHERE id = 701) WHERE id = 701; python scripts/validate_control_source_values.py -> 701 lands in a failing state, not baselined, exit non-zero

break_it.scenario: Backup table left over from an earlier run silently fails to cover this run's rows
break_it.what_happens: the printed rollback would restore only the old run's rows — partial, unnoticed
break_it.how: both repair scripts assert every planned id exists in the backup table AFTER the CTAS and abort before any UPDATE if not (cb701 backed_up check, missing_primary unnest check)
break_it.repro: CREATE TABLE dcp_setback_controls_cb701_repair_20260803 AS SELECT * FROM dcp_setback_controls WHERE FALSE; then run --apply -> 'NOT in backup ... Aborting before any UPDATE', exit 2

break_it.scenario: A genuinely truncated 400-char quote whose cut lands right after a full stop gets judged as complete evidence
break_it.what_happens: a verdict (pass OR flag) is issued from severed evidence — luck reported as verification
break_it.how: services/extracted_data_integrity.py:733 — length == 400 is TRUNCATED_EVIDENCE regardless of terminal punctuation
break_it.repro: pytest tests/test_control_source_values.py -k punctuation -> asserts evidence_is_truncated('x'*399 + '.') is True; fails on the pre-change code

break_it.scenario: The re-filed secondary_street_setback rows vanish from the UI because no display map knows the new slug
break_it.what_happens: 20 served corner-lot controls render under 'Other' with a raw snake_case slug, or a consumer keying on the label drops them
break_it.how: structured-controls route.ts CONTROL_CATEGORIES + CONTROL_TYPE_LABELS entries (Setbacks, order 1) and SEE CATEGORY_MAP entry; vocabulary sync test pins SQL + Python + live DB together
break_it.repro: git checkout HEAD~1 -- frontend-nextjs/app/api/dcp/structured-controls/route.ts; GET /api/dcp/structured-controls for a parramatta corner-lot property -> category 'Other', label 'secondary_street_setback'

break_it.scenario: The dup-check before each INSERT of a missing primary misses, so a re-run duplicates the ryde front 6.0 row and doubles the council's served front controls
break_it.what_happens: capacity/conveyancing reads would see two served front setbacks for ryde dwelling_house
break_it.how: missing_primary dup-check on (lga, dev_type, control_type, condition) skips existing rows; verified by re-running the script post-apply — plans 0 writes

break_it.scenario: The retirement of fairfield 714 leaves secondary-dwelling consumers silently reading the retired 6.0m
break_it.what_happens: a consumer without an is_current filter would still serve the narrow-lot garage value as a granny-flat front setback
break_it.how: every serving read path filters is_current (capacity route ts:348, conveyancing fetch_dcp_setbacks per the DQ-35 fix); the detector prints served=False for 714 and the row's review_reason states the ruling
break_it.repro: SELECT is_current FROM dcp_setback_controls WHERE id = 714 -> FALSE; GET structured-controls for a fairfield property -> no secondary_dwelling front_setback row
